package_info.package_name: polyfill.io (CDN service, as used by npm packages such as create-polyfill-service-url and dynamic-polyfill)
package_info.package_manager: npm (and any web project embedding cdn.polyfill.io)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using cdn.polyfill.io after domain transfer to Funnull (Feb 2024 onward)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious JavaScript after a change in domain ownership. The CDN injected code that redirected mobile users to scam sites, affecting any website or npm package embedding scripts from cdn.polyfill.io. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the malicious code was automatically deployed to all dependent sites and packages.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits a website embedding the CDN script
execution_context.file_location: Injected via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"> in website HTML or via npm packages that reference this CDN

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code inspects the browser's user agent string to determine if the visitor is on a mobile device, then forcibly redirects the browser to an attacker-controlled scam domain, resulting in user redirection and exposure to phishing or further malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs user agent sniffing specifically for mobile devices and initiates a forced redirect to an external, attacker-controlled domain. This behavior is not expected in a polyfill library and is a hallmark of web-based supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate polyfill CDN script should only provide JavaScript polyfills for browser compatibility and must not perform user agent checks for malicious purposes or redirect users to unrelated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User agent checks and redirection may be used by first-party scripts to serve mobile-optimized content, but such logic should never be present in a third-party polyfill CDN script, especially one intended solely for compatibility fixes.
key_indicators: User agent sniffing targeting mobile devices within a polyfill script
Forced redirection to an external, non-polyfill, attacker-controlled domain
Malicious logic injected via a widely used third-party CDN
Redirection logic present in a script expected to only provide polyfills

attack_chain.action: A website or npm package embeds the polyfill.io CDN script in their HTML or JavaScript code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is loaded into the user's browser from the compromised CDN.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits the affected website, the malicious JavaScript executes in their browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: The script inspects the user agent to identify mobile users.

attack_chain.action: If the user is on a mobile device, the script forcibly redirects them to a scam or phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: The user is exposed to further attacks, scams, or malware on the attacker-controlled site.

behavioral_signatures: Third-party CDN JavaScript performing user agent sniffing and conditional redirection
Unexpected runtime redirection initiated by polyfill scripts
Polyfill scripts making network requests or redirects to non-polyfill domains
Presence of mobile device detection logic in polyfill CDN scripts
file_indicators: References to cdn.polyfill.io in package source code (e.g., create-polyfill-service-url, dynamic-polyfill)
Any inclusion of cdn.polyfill.io or polyfill.io CDN URLs in HTML or JavaScript files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests or browser redirects to domains not affiliated with polyfill.io, such as scam-redirect.example.com, from pages loading cdn.polyfill.io
Any network traffic initiated by polyfill scripts to domains unrelated to polyfill service
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the inclusion of cdn.polyfill.io scripts in web pages or npm package dependencies. Analyze the runtime behavior of polyfill scripts for user agent sniffing and redirection logic, especially targeting mobile devices. Flag any polyfill script that initiates network requests or redirects to non-polyfill domains. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) and Subresource Integrity (SRI) to restrict and verify third-party scripts. Regularly audit dependencies and block or alert on known-compromised CDN domains. Implement automated scanning for suspicious redirection or network activity originating from polyfill scripts.
